claim: TanStack argues search params are first-class serializable, shareable state that must be schema-validated at the route to avoid drift and broken deep links.
quote: If you're not treating search params like state, you're going to keep leaking it, breaking it, and working around it.

claim: Routes declare search validation via validateSearch (function, Zod, Valibot, or ArkType); useSearch() reads are fully typed, parsed, and defaulted, with fallback() for per-field errors.
quote: The validator can be a function, a Zod schema, or any adapter that conforms to the validator interface.

claim: React Router generates a +types/<route>.d.ts per route via typegen (executing routes.ts), typing params, loaderData and actionData; available only in Framework mode, not Data or Declarative mode.
quote: React Router's type generation executes your route config (app/routes.ts by default) to determine the routes for your app. It then generates a +types/<route file>.d.ts for each route within a special .react-router/types/ directory.

claim: Setting up route module type safety requires rootDirs config plus running react-router typegen so generated .d.ts files resolve next to route modules.
quote: React Router generates route-specific types to power type inference for URL params, loader data, and more.

claim: TanStack Router types search params, path params and loader data with zero config; React Router v7 SPA mode needs manual casts like useLoaderData() as Post and untyped URLSearchParams; bundles ~40KB vs ~32KB.
quote: TanStack Router wins on type safety — search params, path params, and loader data are all fully typed with zero configuration.

claim: TanStack Router delivers end-to-end type safety across route params, search params, loaders, context and Link components at compile time.
quote: TanStack Router provides end-to-end type safety: route params, search params, loaders, context, and Link components are all fully typed at compile time.

claim: To achieve its type safety TanStack Router uses very advanced and complex TypeScript inference and deviates from routing norms.
quote: TanStack Router is designed to be as type-safe as possible by leveraging TypeScript's type system, which involves using very advanced and complex types and type inference.

claim: As features like nested context, loaders and search validation are added, single-file route definitions become infeasible and configuration spreads across many files.
quote: making it infeasible to define routes in a single file

claim: Wouter is a minimal (~2.5KB) hooks-based router exposing useSearch() but no validation or typing layer for search params.
quote: Wouter provides useSearch() but no validation layer.

claim: TanStack Router suits client-heavy SPAs, dashboards, admin panels and search-driven UIs where filters, sorting, pagination and view modes belong in the URL and need typed validated access.
quote: Multiple filters, sorting, pagination, view modes, and combinations of these belong in the URL, and they need validation and typed access.

claim: React Router v7 in framework mode reaches similar type safety to TanStack via a codegen step, but SPA mode requires manual casting.
quote: In framework mode, React Router v7 achieves similar type safety to TanStack Router through a codegen step. However, in SPA mode, manual casting is required.

claim: Third-party library adds validated type safety for all React Router v7 route parts (path params, search params, state, hash) on both building and parsing URLs.
quote: Enhanced type safety via validation for all route params in React Router v7.

claim: TypeRoute is a 4kB type-safe React router with full autocomplete and simple setup, an alternative to full-framework routers.
quote: Type-safe React router that just works - simple setup, full autocomplete, 4kB gzipped

claim: TanStack Router serializes search with JSON.stringify/JSON.parse by default so numbers, booleans, arrays and nested objects round-trip through the URL without manual coercion.
quote: TanStack Router serializes search with JSON.stringify/JSON.parse by default, so numbers, booleans, arrays, and nested objects round-trip through the URL without manual coercion.

claim: React Router is the incumbent router with the largest ecosystem and lowest migration friction for existing React Router codebases.
quote: React Router v7 represents the merging of React Router and Remix into a single package.
